title_zh: 用于安全机器人控制的框架化编程智能体
one_line: External obstacle-box route verification and contact-aware execution improve safe manipulation over the same coding agents, with component ablations and counted real-robot trials.
one_line_zh: 框外验路与避障接触提高安全操作，组件消融和计数真机试验验证。

online_eval.quote: We evaluate SafeHarness on all 32 SafeLIBERO tasks with 10 seeds per task, and on real-robot using PiPER-X 6-DoF research arm for two tasks with 20 trials each.

strong_baselines.quote: Since both share backbone, tools, and skill memory, the gains isolate the harnesses.

budget_matched.quote: On SafeLIBERO, an episode is allowed at most 900 environment steps; a successful run takes about 400 steps on average, and about 700 on Libero-10, whose tasks comprise two sub-goals.

component_ablation.quote: When a component is removed, the corresponding phase is left to the agent itself: MS + Route lets the agent perform grasp and release on its own, and MS + Contact lets it plan its own transport motions.

validator_check.quote: The verifier evaluates a single condition, namely whether the route intersects the obstacle, and it does so on an approximately measured scene.

evidence_level.quote: We evaluate SafeHarness on all 32 SafeLIBERO tasks with 10 seeds per task, and on real-robot using PiPER-X 6-DoF research arm for two tasks with 20 trials each.

S1.quote: Before any motion is issued, it is checked against the obstacle box outside the language model; the check covers the gripper and, when an object is held, the object as well.

S2.quote: The target and the obstacle are grounded as bounding boxes by a segmentation model. On that view the model is asked for a route as a polyline of waypoints

S3.quote: The verifier evaluates a single condition, namely whether the route intersects the obstacle, and it does so on an approximately measured scene.

F1.quote: Other physical constraints that arise during execution fall outside its scope, and a route that passes verification may still fail against them.

AP6.quote: A route released for execution carries, however, only a limited guarantee. The verifier evaluates a single condition, namely whether the route intersects the obstacle, and it does so on an approximately measured scene.
